evidence.reason: At the tip, run()'s automatic path calls drain() and silently normalizes a None return to {'status': 'drained'} with exit 0 (apps/crq-python/crq_repair.py:1677-1680). The same function already distinguishes early exits with structured statuses and reasons: 'disabled', 'paused' (peak blackout / rate limit), 'busy' (service.lock), and 'deferred' with the fetch error text (lines 1637-1668). In particular the recover path converts a fetch_clone error into {'status':'deferred','reason':error[:200]} (1660-1663), and the comment at 1664-1665 confirms fetch_clone can fail or wait on the tick lock, so drain() returning None for those cases is folded into the same 'drained' result as a completed pass. That is a real, minor machine-mode reporting defect: a JSON consumer cannot tell that no inbox work ran, and an operational failure is reported as a normal drained outcome with exit 0. The smallest compatible fix is to propagate the existing structured status/reason (deferred/paused/busy) instead of returning 'drained'; no new 'refused' vocabulary or contract clause is required, and exit codes for non-error statuses stay unchanged.
